references.text: Sodom and Gomorrah are used as examples of God's judgment and destruction due to sin, providing context for the metaphor of Sodom's winters.
Isaiah refers to Israel's leaders as rulers of Sodom, using similar imagery to describe moral corruption.
Isaiah's parable of the vineyard that produces wild grapes uses similar imagery about fruit symbolizing evil instead of righteousness.
Jeremiah uses the image of a noble vine that has been transformed into an alien, wild plant, echoing themes of corruption.
Ezekiel compares Jerusalem to Sodom and describes their sins, linking together the theme of moral decay.
Hosea describes Israel as a fruitful vine that bears fruit for itself, reflecting similar themes of corrupted fruit.
Jesus teaches that a bad tree bears bad fruit, using similar imagery about fruit revealing inner character.
Paul quotes about poison and bitterness from the tongue, connecting to the image of poisonous and bitter fruit.
